definitions.title: Continuity at an Interior Point
definitions.statement: A function f is continuous at an interior point c of its domain if: (1) f(c) is defined, (2) lim_{x->c} f(x) exists, and (3) lim_{x->c} f(x) = f(c).
conditions: c must be in the domain of f
Two-sided limit exists as a finite real number
definitions.explanation: Continuity means there is no interruption, break, jump, or hole in the graph at x = c.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Continuity requires value exists, limit exists, and value equals limit.

definitions.title: Intermediate Value Theorem (IVT)
definitions.latex: f(a) < y_0 < f(b) \implies \exists c \in (a, b) \text{ s.t. } f(c) = y_0
definitions.statement: If f is continuous on a closed interval [a, b], and y0 is any value strictly between f(a) and f(b), then there exists at least one value c in (a, b) such that f(c) = y0.
conditions: f must be continuous on the entire closed interval [a, b]
y0 is strictly between f(a) and f(b)
definitions.explanation: A continuous curve cannot jump over any intermediate value. Applied frequently to guarantee roots when f(a) and f(b) have opposite signs.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Continuous functions attain every intermediate value between their endpoint values.

definitions.title: Classification of Discontinuities
definitions.latex: \text{Removable: } \lim f(x) \neq f(c); \quad \text{Jump: } \lim_{x \to c^+} f \neq \lim_{x \to c^-} f; \quad \text{Infinite: } \lim f = \pm \infty
definitions.statement: Discontinuities are classified as: (1) Removable (limit exists but != f(c)), (2) Jump (left and right limits exist but are unequal), (3) Infinite (one or both one-sided limits are infinite).
conditions: At least one of the three continuity conditions fails at c
definitions.explanation: Removable discontinuities can be fixed by defining or redefining a single point. Jump and infinite discontinuities cannot be removed.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Discontinuities are either removable (holes) or essential (jumps and vertical asymptotes).
